text:
toni: heads up - found a weird routing behavior causing quota metrics for one org to show under another org in the console billing view. repro in staging after a canary of the quota-router change.

rahul: can you share the exact API call? is this the /billing/usage endpoint?

toni: yes /api/billing/usage?range=30d . steps: fetch for org A in console, then rapidly switch tenant to B and open billing -> some charts show A's numbers.

anna: maybe quota-router uses a routing table that keys by ip or pod rather than tenant header. we recently added a fallback to route to lastSeenTenant for websocket reconnections.

toni: logs show upstream call had header X-Tenant: B but router forwarded to pod handling A with header set to A internally.

rahul: quick fix: ensure proxy preserves X-Tenant header and that routing decisions use the request header not an external sticky map. Also add a guard: if resolved tenant != header tenant, log with severity and increment `routing_tenant_mismatch`.

anna: also rolling back the quota-router change for canary pods helps. i've rolled it back to 0% while we investigate.

sre-bot: rollback successful on canary pool.

toni: follow-ups: rahul will push header-preserve patch, anna will scan other routers for similar fallback logic, and i'll add the telemetry + dashboard.

rahul: pushing patch now. small change to proxy: `preserve_incoming_headers = true` and assert in unit tests. also adding an integration test that simulates rapid tenant switch and ensures no mismatches.

toni: thanks. adding this to postmortem if we see prod incidents.
